predecessors.name: Yuan dynasty
predecessors.text: Yunnan without the Dali district, which Duan Shi held as the last hereditary Governor-General of Dali (Ming conquest of Yunnan page)

successors.name: Ming dynasty
successors.text: Yunnan without the Dali district, which Duan Shi held as the last hereditary Governor-General of Dali (Ming conquest of Yunnan page)

ledger.x: 1368: the Yuan viceroy of Yunnan holds the province for the Yuan after the court leaves China.
6 January 1382: Basalawarmi kills himself after the decisive defeat of his army.
6 January 1382: the Principality of Liang ends with the death of Basalawarmi and Yunnan passes to the Ming.

wars.name: Ming conquest of Yunnan
wars.outcome: Ming victory: Basalawarmi's army (about 100,000) is defeated by about 300,000 Ming troops in 1381 and he dies by suicide on 6 January 1382; Duan Shi's Dali falls in 1382 and its last stronghold, Dengchuan, in February 1383.

wars.name: Red Turban Rebellions
wars.outcome: Umbrella conflict; Yunnan stays Yuan until 1381.

certainty.note: A Mongol viceroy holding a province; the pages name Yunnan, Kunming and Dali but no frontier line.
